subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/gem: Skip writeback of shmem folios with extra references

reviews.author: Andi Shyti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Andi Shyti noted that the patch does not handle the case where a folio has extra references beyond the page cache and writeback_iter(), which can lead to stale TLB entries allowing writes through, and requested checking for this condition in addition to the existing folio_mapped() check.

Reviewer Andi Shyti pointed out that the patch is unnecessary because the i915 writeback iterator already skips shmem folios in the described case, making the new refcount check redundant.
reviews.raw_body:

writeback iterator already skips the shmem folio in the case you
describe, so the new refcount check doesn't change the outcome.

Thanks,
Andi

reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of a folio being written through a stale TLB entry after it has been unmapped, and suggested adding a check for folios with references beyond the page cache and writeback_iter().

2026-11-19.patch_summary: This patch modifies the drm/i915/gem module to skip writeback of shmem folios that have extra references, preventing a race condition where a stale TLB entry can still store data to an unmapped folio until the TLB is flushed. The change ensures that such folios are left to reclaim as mapped ones would be, rather than being written back from swap without the stored data.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author realized that __shmem_writeback() never runs for shmem folios due to PAGECACHE_TAG_DIRTY not being set, and questions the purpose of writeback in this context.
reviews.raw_body:
Oh. It took me a while to see why.

__shmem_writeback() asks writeback_iter() for PAGECACHE_TAG_DIRTY
folios, and shmem never sets that tag, its ->dirty_folio is
noop_dirty_folio(). So the loop body never runs for any folio, and
hasn't since 776a853a43c9 ("i915: Use writeback_iter()").

That makes me question the whole writeback thing. What's going on
there, and what's the plan?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

2026-11-20.patch_summary: This patch modifies the drm/i915/gem module to skip writeback of shmem folios that have extra references, preventing a race condition where a stale TLB entry can still store data to an unmapped folio until the TLB is flushed. The change ensures that such folios are left to reclaim as mapped ones would be, rather than being written back from swap without the stored data.

a half is a pretty good indicator that this instance should simply
go away.

reviews.author: Joonas Lahtinen
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Joonas Lahtinen expressed frustration that patches are being pushed without proper review and maintenance, specifically mentioning the introduction of regressions and lack of Cc'ing maintainers.

Reviewer Joonas Lahtinen expressed strong disagreement with the patch, citing that the writeback for dirty shmem pages was a complex issue that took multiple years to address and is more likely to occur on older hardware. He questioned whether the patch's authors would take responsibility for reverting or fixing the potential issues it may cause.
reviews.raw_body:
Not so funny to me, you folks are pushing regressions without ever
Cc'ing a single maintainer in the original patches.

I was under impression that Linux development had some rules about
not introducing regressions and also some rules about not pushing
stuff silently to other subsystems. Maybe it's just me not able to
keep up with the vibes of these times.

---

That's not a good indicator in this case.

The writeback for dirty shmem pages took multiple years and multiple
iterations to address the best we could as it's not exactly a race
that shows up frequently.

It's also more likely on the hardware from the era the fix was developed
on, and the owners of those older machines are not exactly jumping to the
latest mainline but rather more likely to run Debian oldstable.

So which one of you will be writing up a revert or fix for the offending
patch or do you expect us to clean up the mess you've created?

Regards, Joonas

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary:
The reviewer expressed frustration that the patch's author did not properly CC the DRM and i915 mailing lists, which he believes is a common issue with core fixes.

Reviewer Christoph Hellwig expressed frustration that the patch was submitted without addressing the underlying issue first, and requested a more collaborative approach from the submitter.
reviews.raw_body:
Nothing here was silent.  All the relevant lists were on Cc, but as
so often with core fixes the drm and i915 folks completely ignored it.

---

Of course no one is going to revert this.  The change was part of an
important and invasive core change that is not going to get reverted
for something that hasn't seen any single bug report.

In genral everyone on the mm/writeback/pagecache/shmem side is happy
to work on a solution, but a little bit less of an attitude helps to
get things done.
